candidates.label: Italy (Augustan Italy, label point)
candidates.support: Italy's identity and extent under Roman rule are undisputed; the coordinate is Wikidata's representative point for Roman Italy, near the peninsula's center.

summary.text: Italy was the Roman homeland, the peninsula containing Rome itself. Rather than being one of the senatorial or imperial provinces Augustus divided among the Senate and himself in 27 BC, it kept a privileged status as the home territory of Roman citizens. Rome, the capital, and Puteoli, a major port on Italy's southern coast where Paul's ship landed on the way to Rome, both appear in Acts, and Hebrews closes with a greeting 'from those in Italy.'

history.text: Italy is absent from Cassius Dio's list of the provinces Augustus divided between the Senate and himself in 27 BC; per later scholarship, Augustus instead organized Italy itself into eleven regions, administered apart from the ordinary provincial system.

Acts records that Priscilla and Aquila had 'recently come from Italy' because 'Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome'; Suetonius likewise reports that Claudius 'expelled' the Jews from Rome over disturbances instigated by 'Chrestus,' an edict most historians date to about AD 49, just before this project's 'about AD 50' date.

When it was determined that we should sail for Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan band.
From there we circled around and arrived at Rhegium. After one day, a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
